NEW YORK CITY COUNCIL STATED MEETING 29 passed in my district and a hero that we lost not only within the city but within the state. Dr. John Flateau, who many of you know, especially after this past redistricting, was a good man and a great man, but much more than leading the Redistricting Commission, he was a constituent, partner, an advisor, and a friend. Perhaps most importantly what set Dr. Flateau apart is that he truly was committed to the success of his community, his city, and his people - Black people across the diaspora. This body recognized the former member, the late Al Vann, last year; Dr. Flateau worked for and closely with him, along with New York’s first Black mayor, David Dinkins. And whenever there has been Black greatness in Brooklyn, Dr. Flateau’s influence was never far away. Much of the equity we have achieved, and even what is yet to come, is thanks in large part to Dr. Flateau. I and all of Brooklyn am so very sorry to have lost him, and I extend my deepest condolences to his family. MAJORITY LEADER FARÍAS: Seeing no other members signed up for General Discussion, I will now call on Speaker Adrienne Adams to close today’s Stated Meeting.

Thank you, Madam Majority Leader. Apologies to our amazing Senior Pastor Bishop Rice. Bishop Calvin Rice, Senior Pastor of the New Jerusalem Worship Center in Jamaica, Queens is a dedicated and selfless faith leader who has served our communities in southeast Queens for many years. He has advanced educational opportunities for our young scholars, led the restoration of residential housing, and supported underserved neighborhoods across the City. Bishop Rice continues to give back to this city through his expertise and leadership on numerous civil rights, nonprofit and community organizations. He is well-regarded and admired for his distinguished service. I am honored to have known and worked with Bishop Rice for many years. He is a stalwart, revered leader in my district, the Great 28.
